units.en: Air technologies are used to ⟦0⟧, unlock, and improve different types of aircraft. They are divided into eight different aircraft types: fighters, close air support, naval bombers, heavy fighters, tactical bombers, strategic bombers, scout planes, and transport planes. Each non-jet fighter, close air support, and naval bomber model also has a carrier variant that can be researched. These variants are able to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.
For available missions per aircraft type, see ⟦0⟧.

With the introduction of special projects in ⟦0⟧ and the accompanying ⟦1⟧, all air technologies now also generate aerodynamics and avionics breakthrough progress while being researched. Air technologies are particularly intertwined with the ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ special projects, which act as prerequisites for many later technologies in the tree.

Inter-War FighterWhile fighter aircraft underwent many changes through the Great War, and since, the bi-plane design is becoming obsolete. We must begin to translate civilian technological advances into military applications.
Inter-War Carrier FighterAn early fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Fighter ILight airframes have been revolutionized with the introduction of radial engines, monoplane designs and all metal skin construction. This design is our attempt at creating our first modern fighter plane.
Carrier Fighter IAn early fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Fighter IIThe pace of fighter advancements is astounding, and as such, we must continue to incorporate the technology as well as improve upon existing concepts. Our new fighter design must be capable of high speed, high performance at altitude and the best range possible. Additionally, it must be very well armed.
Enables Unlocks Jet Engine special project
Carrier Fighter IIAn improved fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Fighter IIIWhile our previous generations of fighter plane have proven worthy, any advantage gained by a better design should be taken. This aircraft will be the pinnacle platform of piston-engined fighter that will have excellent power, high agility, deadly weaponry and good range.
Carrier Fighter IIIAn advanced fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Jet Fighter IPrevious increases in speed pale in comparison to the introduction of the first jet fighters. While we have yet to learn how to best construct planes for these engines, regular fighter planes cannot compete.
⟦0⟧ One of: Close Air Support III Fighter III Naval Bomber III
Close Air Support III Fighter III Naval Bomber III
Enables Unlocks Axial Jet Engine special project
Jet Fighter IINew swept wing designs and lighter material choices will allow us to extend the range and speed of the revolutionary jet fighters even further.

Close Air Support IOur CAS doctrine requires an aircraft capable of precision surface attack. While these aircraft carry a lesser payload compared to our larger Tactical Bombers, they are capable of attacking and destroying small targets of opportunity through strafing and dive bombing.
Carrier Close Air Support IAn early close air support plane modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Close Air Support IIEarly war experiences have shown that increased speed, armor and maneuverability are necessary for CAS aircraft survivability against enemy fighters and ground fire. This next generation of ground attack aircraft will also utilize larger bombs, cannons and machineguns to inflict greater damage to their targets.
Carrier Close Air Support IIAn improved close air support plane modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Close Air Support IIIThe ever increasing capability of target AA and enemy interceptors require further evolution of our CAS aircraft. The new design incorporates increased engine power, airframe improvements for increased diving capability and protection, as well as even greater payloads.
Carrier Close Air Support IIIAn advanced close air support plane modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Naval Bomber INaval aviation will be vital in the coming decade to confront new developments in naval warfare, such as the increased importance of submarines. Seaplanes with capacity to work as dive bombers and recon vehicles will be of use.
Carrier Naval Bomber IAn early naval bomber modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.
Naval Bomber IINew engine technology and aerodynamically refined designs will boost the speed and diving attack capability of naval planes significantly.
Carrier Naval Bomber IIAn improved naval bomber modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.
Naval Bomber IIIAll-metal designs and powerful airbrakes allow for more complex naval aeronautics. The planes of the future will demand a larger crew to operate these advanced systems, however.
Carrier Naval Bomber IIIAn advanced naval bomber modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Inter-War BomberIt is widely believed that the next war will be won entirely by bombing the enemy to extinction. It is imperative that we begin designing our own bomber plane that is capable of carrying heavy payloads at adequate speed.

Tactical Bomber IMedium bombers need to be versatile and fast, capable of fulfilling a range of roles. A twin-engined design, remaining relatively light, can continue to be of use for many years to come.
Tactical Bomber IIHeavier designs of tactical bombers can extend range, payload and speed while maintaining the planes' capacity to perform a wide variety of missions.
Enables Unlocks Jet Engine special project Bouncing Bomb special project

Tactical Bomber IIITaking a page from the advancements in fighter planes, unconventional materials and shapes can make new designs some of the fastest and best performing twin-engine planes ever built.

Jet Tactical Bomber IThe advent of jet fighters necessitates bombers that can outrun or at least match their speed. First-generation medium bombers and bomber-fighters equipped with jet engines will fill this role.
Jet Tactical Bomber IINot content with speed, future jet bombers will set altitude and range records, delivering payloads and performing reconnaissance on intercontinental missions.

Heavy Fighter IOur bomber force needs escort protection from enemy fighters all the way to their targets and back. In order to provide this escort, we must design fighter aircraft with bomber range. Out of necessity these aircraft are larger, slower and less agile than light fighters, though they can carry significant armament.

Heavy Fighter IIThe war has taught us that our heavy fighter design is vulnerable to more nimble fighters, but quite good at the interception of enemy bombers due to heavy armament. This next design will focus on increased attack capability against enemy aircraft and even ground targets. Its speed and range will be improved as well.

Heavy Fighter IIIThough our heavy fighter force has shown adeptness in various roles, we must consider a new design that will enhance its ability relative to enemy fighters, as well as allow it to continue intercepting increasingly faster and better defended enemy bombers.

Scout Plane IGathering intelligence on enemy troop movements and providing reports of enemy naval deployments has been the original mission for airplanes since their first deployment in the Great War, and is still an important mission.

Scout Plane IIBy developing dedicated planes for aerial surveillance and long-range reconnaissance, we ensure that we gain and maintain an accurate picture of our opponent's intentions and capabilities.

Strategic Bomber IExperiences from the Great War and studies since show that bombing the enemy's military targets and major cities will win the next war. At the very least, we must have a bomber capable of delivering such destruction. It will need to fly high and at good speed, and it must carry a large payload. This will require a large airframe with multiple engines. It will also have some defensive capability.

Strategic Bomber IIBombing has proven effective at reducing the enemy's capacity to wage war. More defensive weaponry and increased speed will allow a new design to avoid destruction, while increasing the payload and range will make it more effective.
Enables Unlocks Intercontinental Bomber special project Mothership Aircraft special project Bouncing Bomb special project Earthshaker Bomb special project

Strategic Bomber IIITo avoid losses to enemy fighters and ground fire, our next design will fly at great altitude. It will be larger to carry both an enormous payload and more fuel, to increase range.
Jet Strategic Bomber IMultiple jet engines allow new designs unprecedented speed while maintaining a large payload and long range. These planes are built for a new era of weapons of mass destruction.

Reinforced Mothership WingsWithout their mothership, the fighters are essentially stranded in the air, severely limiting their operational effectiveness. Strengthening the mothership's air wings is the most cost-effective strategy to enhance the survivability of the entire squadron.
Götterdämmerung Mothership Aircraft Strategic Bomber II
Miniature FightersWith smaller fighters we will be able to carry more of them into battle without sacrificing much firepower, as well as reducing the weight of the Motherships load
Upgrades Mothership Aircraft: Air Attack: +6% Agility: +6% Fuel Usage: -8%
Aerial HangarsAerial Hangars attached to the mothership allows us to fit even more miniature fighters onto the top of the aircraft, allowing for increased firepower and further reach.
Upgrades Mothership Aircraft: Range: +20% Air Attack: +10% Agility: +10%

Improved Transport PlanePlanes used to transport troops on paradrop missions.
Modern Transport PlanePlanes used to transport troops on paradrop missions.
Centrifugal JetCentrifugal jets use a single stage compressor to compress the intake air, before blasting it out to create thrust. This results in smaller, more easily maintained engines.
